blocks.en: 📖 Evangelism — Unit 7: Personal Evangelism
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Evangelismo — Unidad 7: Evangelismo Personal

blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary · Dr. Wayne Cook, Author and Professor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Seminary Director
blocks.es_reference: Seminario Teológico de Chapala · Dr. Wayne Cook, Autor y Profesor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Director del Seminario

blocks.en: Orientation: The Most Basic Form of Gospel Proclamation
blocks.es_reference: Orientación: La Forma Más Básica de Proclamación del Evangelio

blocks.en: While evangelism may take place in many settings — public preaching, crusades, broadcast — the most common and often most effective form is personal evangelism. This is the one-on-one communication of the gospel within the context of everyday life. It is not an event but a lifestyle. It occurs in conversations, relationships, and ordinary moments. It allows for deeper understanding, personal engagement, and meaningful response.
blocks.es_reference: Si bien el evangelismo puede tener lugar en muchos entornos — predicación pública, cruzadas, transmisión — la forma más común y a menudo más eficaz es el evangelismo personal. Esta es la comunicación uno a uno del evangelio dentro del contexto de la vida cotidiana. No es un evento sino un estilo de vida. Ocurre en conversaciones, relaciones y momentos ordinarios. Permite una comprensión más profunda, un compromiso personal y una respuesta significativa.

blocks.en: Every believer can engage in personal evangelism. The shy can listen and ask questions. The outgoing can initiate conversations. The intellectual can answer objections. The compassionate can serve and then speak. This unit covers Jesus' example, a tool for reading where a person actually stands, and the practical principles of listening, questioning, boldness, sensitivity, readiness, and dependence on the Spirit.
blocks.es_reference: Todo creyente puede participar en el evangelismo personal. El tímido puede escuchar y hacer preguntas. El extrovertido puede iniciar conversaciones. El intelectual puede responder a las objeciones. El compasivo puede servir y luego hablar. Esta unidad cubre el ejemplo de Jesús, una herramienta para discernir dónde está realmente una persona, y los principios prácticos de escuchar, preguntar, valentía, sensibilidad, prontitud y dependencia del Espíritu Santo.

blocks.en: I. The Example of Christ
blocks.es_reference: I. El Ejemplo de Cristo

blocks.en: Jesus often engaged individuals personally. In John 4, He spoke with the Samaritan woman — a person of different ethnicity, gender, and moral reputation. The conversation began naturally: "Jesus said to her, 'Give Me a drink'" (John 4:7, NKJV). From that simple request He moved to spiritual truth, exposed her need, and revealed Himself as the Messiah. In John 3, He spoke with Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler of the Jews. Here the approach was different — more direct, more theological — but the goal was the same: to lead him to new birth. Different people, different approaches, same truth.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús a menudo se relacionaba con personas individualmente. En Juan 4, habló con la mujer samaritana — una persona de etnia, género y reputación moral diferentes. La conversación comenzó naturalmente: "Jesús le dijo: Dame de beber" (Juan 4:7, RVG). A partir de esa simple solicitud, pasó a la verdad espiritual, expuso su necesidad y se reveló como el Mesías. En Juan 3, habló con Nicodemo, un fariseo y principal de los judíos. Aquí el enfoque fue diferente — más directo, más teológico — pero el objetivo era el mismo: llevarlo al nuevo nacimiento. Diferentes personas, diferentes enfoques, la misma verdad.

blocks.en: Notice what Jesus did not do. He did not wait for people to come to a synagogue service. He went to them — at a well, in a house, on a road. He did not deliver a one-size-fits-all sermon; He read the person and adjusted His approach. Personal evangelism follows that pattern. It goes where people are, listens to where they are, and speaks accordingly.
blocks.es_reference: Note lo que Jesús no hizo. No esperó a que las personas vinieran a un culto en la sinagoga. Fue a ellas — a un pozo, a una casa, a un camino. No predicó un sermón uniforme; leyó a la persona y ajustó Su enfoque. El evangelismo personal sigue ese patrón. Va donde las personas están, escucha dónde están y habla en consecuencia.

blocks.en: II. Reading the Person: Robinson's Five Levels of Response
blocks.es_reference: II. Leer a la Persona: Los Cinco Niveles de Respuesta de Robinson

blocks.en: Not every conversation begins from the same starting point. Darrell Robinson of the Home Mission Board identified five levels of response to the gospel. The wise personal evangelist learns to identify which level the hearer occupies and adjusts his approach accordingly.
blocks.es_reference: No toda conversación comienza desde el mismo punto de partida. Darrell Robinson, de la Junta de Misiones Domésticas, identificó cinco niveles de respuesta al evangelio. El evangelista personal sabio aprende a identificar el nivel en el que se encuentra el oyente y ajusta su enfoque en consecuencia.

blocks.en: Robinson's Five Levels
blocks.es_reference: Los Cinco Niveles de Robinson

blocks.en: Ignorant. They know nothing about the gospel. They must be taught. Begin with God, sin, Christ, response. Do not assume vocabulary.
blocks.es_reference: Ignorantes. No saben nada sobre el evangelio. Deben ser enseñados. Comience con Dios, el pecado, Cristo, la respuesta. No asuma vocabulario.

blocks.en: Indifferent. They have heard the gospel story but are apathetic toward it. They must be stirred to make a response — through questions, urgency, or a confronting illustration.
blocks.es_reference: Indiferentes. Han oído la historia del evangelio pero son apáticos hacia ella. Deben ser provocados a una respuesta — mediante preguntas, urgencia o una ilustración confrontante.

blocks.en: Hostile. They have heard and rejected the gospel and are antagonistic. They must be met with love and listening. Robinson counsels: rather than reacting in anger, be a good listener. Among Muslim communities in Togo, missionaries have used Old Testament storying — premature introduction of Christ gets the missionary thrown out of the village; patient storying opens hearts over time.
blocks.es_reference: Hostiles. Han oído y rechazado el evangelio y son antagonistas. Deben ser recibidos con amor y escucha. Robinson aconseja: en lugar de reaccionar con ira, sea un buen oyente. Entre las comunidades musulmanas de Togo, los misioneros han usado la narración del Antiguo Testamento — la introducción prematura de Cristo hace que el misionero sea expulsado del pueblo; la narración paciente abre corazones con el tiempo.

blocks.en: Interested. They have heard about the gospel and want to know more. They must be cultivated — given time, answers, and follow-up — until they are ready.
blocks.es_reference: Interesados. Han oído sobre el evangelio y quieren saber más. Deben ser cultivados — dándoles tiempo, respuestas y seguimiento — hasta que estén listos.

blocks.en: Ready. They have heard the gospel and want to accept Christ immediately. The evangelist's job here is simple: lead them in prayer to repent of sin, ask forgiveness, and invite Christ as Lord and Savior.
blocks.es_reference: Listos. Han oído el evangelio y quieren aceptar a Cristo inmediatamente. El trabajo del evangelista aquí es sencillo: guiarlos en oración para arrepentirse del pecado, pedir perdón e invitar a Cristo como Señor y Salvador.

blocks.en: A mistake common to new evangelists is treating every conversation as if the person were at level five. Some are. Most are not. A hostile hearer pressed for immediate decision becomes more hostile. An ignorant hearer asked to "pray the prayer" prays words he does not understand. The Spirit gives discernment about which level the person occupies and how to proceed.
blocks.es_reference: Un error común entre los evangelistas nuevos es tratar cada conversación como si la persona estuviera en el nivel cinco. Algunas están. La mayoría no. Un oyente hostil presionado a una decisión inmediata se vuelve más hostil. Un oyente ignorante invitado a "hacer la oración" reza palabras que no entiende. El Espíritu Santo da discernimiento sobre el nivel en el que está la persona y cómo proceder.

blocks.en: III. The Importance of Listening
blocks.es_reference: III. La Importancia de Escuchar

blocks.en: Effective personal evangelism begins with listening. James instructs, "let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak" (James 1:19, NKJV). Listening serves several purposes. It helps identify the person's level on Robinson's scale. It reveals misconceptions that need to be addressed. It builds trust — people are more likely to listen to someone who has first listened to them.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo personal eficaz comienza con escuchar. Santiago instruye: "Todo hombre sea pronto para oír, tardo para hablar" (Santiago 1:19, RVG). Escuchar sirve para varios propósitos. Ayuda a identificar el nivel de la persona en la escala de Robinson. Revela conceptos erróneos que deben abordarse. Genera confianza — es más probable que las personas escuchen a alguien que primero las ha escuchado.

blocks.en: Listening also models humility. The evangelist is not a lecturer delivering a monologue; he is a fellow human being engaging a conversation. He may learn that the person has been hurt by a church, confused by a cult, or has simply never heard the gospel clearly explained. That knowledge shapes how he presents the truth.
blocks.es_reference: Escuchar también modela humildad. El evangelista no es un conferenciante dando un monólogo; es un ser humano comprometido en una conversación. Puede aprender que la persona ha sido herida por una iglesia, confundida por una secta, o simplemente nunca ha oído el evangelio explicado con claridad. Ese conocimiento moldea cómo presenta la verdad.

blocks.en: IV. Asking Diagnostic Questions
blocks.es_reference: IV. Hacer Preguntas de Diagnóstico

blocks.en: Questions often open the door to deeper conversation. Jesus asked, "But who do you say that I am?" (Matthew 16:15, NKJV) — forcing His disciples to move from hearsay to personal conviction. In personal evangelism, diagnostic questions are especially valuable. The two CWT questions are the classic example: "Have you come to the place in your life where you know for certain that you have eternal life?" and "If you were to stand before God and He asked, 'Why should I let you into my heaven?' what would you say?"
blocks.es_reference: Las preguntas a menudo abren la puerta a una conversación más profunda. Jesús preguntó: "¿Y vosotros, quién decís que soy yo?" (Mateo 16:15, RVG) — obligando a Sus discípulos a pasar de los rumores a la convicción personal. En el evangelismo personal, las preguntas de diagnóstico son especialmente valiosas. Las dos preguntas del CWT son el ejemplo clásico: "¿Ha llegado al punto en su vida en que sabe con certeza que tiene vida eterna?" y "Si estuviera de pie ante Dios y Él le preguntara: '¿Por qué debería dejarte entrar en mi cielo?' ¿qué le respondería?"

blocks.en: These two questions reveal where the person actually trusts for salvation — works, religion, sincerity, or Christ alone. A person who answers, "I've tried to live a good life," has just told the evangelist that he is trusting in works. The conversation can now move where it needs to go. Good questions also create curiosity. When a person cannot answer a question, he may become open to hearing the answer.
blocks.es_reference: Estas dos preguntas revelan dónde la persona realmente confía para su salvación — obras, religión, sinceridad o Cristo solo. Una persona que responde: "He tratado de vivir una buena vida", acaba de decirle al evangelista que confía en las obras. La conversación ahora puede ir hacia donde necesita ir. Las buenas preguntas también generan curiosidad. Cuando una persona no puede responder a una pregunta, puede abrirse a oír la respuesta.

blocks.en: V. Boldness and Sensitivity
blocks.es_reference: V. Valentía y Sensibilidad

blocks.en: Personal evangelism requires both boldness and sensitivity. Boldness means speaking truth without apology — Paul asked the Ephesians to pray "that I may open my mouth boldly to make known the mystery of the gospel" (Ephesians 6:19, NKJV). Sensitivity means delivering that truth with grace — "Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt" (Colossians 4:6, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo personal requiere tanto valentía como sensibilidad. Valentía significa hablar la verdad sin disculpa — Pablo pidió a los efesios que oraran "para que al abrir mi boca me sea dada palabra para dar a conocer con denuedo el misterio del evangelio" (Efesios 6:19, RVG). Sensibilidad significa entregar esa verdad con gracia — "Sea vuestra palabra siempre con gracia, sazonada con sal" (Colosenses 4:6, RVG).

blocks.en: Boldness without wisdom is harsh and drives people away. Sensitivity without boldness is silent and fails to confront sin or call for decision. The biblical balance is found in genuine love. When love governs the conversation, boldness is not rudeness and sensitivity is not cowardice. The goal is "speaking the truth in love" (Ephesians 4:15, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: La valentía sin sabiduría es áspera y aleja a las personas. La sensibilidad sin valentía es silenciosa y no confronta el pecado ni llama a la decisión. El equilibrio bíblico se encuentra en el amor genuino. Cuando el amor gobierna la conversación, la valentía no es grosería y la sensibilidad no es cobardía. La meta es "siguiendo la verdad en amor" (Efesios 4:15, RVG).

blocks.en: VI. Recognizing Open Doors: When People Are Most Receptive
blocks.es_reference: VI. Reconocer Puertas Abiertas: Cuándo las Personas Son Más Receptivas

blocks.en: Opportunities for personal evangelism arise in daily life, but they are not uniformly distributed. People are most receptive to the gospel during seasons of change. Three categories deserve special attention.
blocks.es_reference: Las oportunidades para el evangelismo personal surgen en la vida diaria, pero no están distribuidas uniformemente. Las personas son más receptivas al evangelio durante temporadas de cambio. Tres categorías merecen atención especial.

blocks.en: Transitions. Immigrants, the newly married, the newly retired, new parents, the newly bereaved — anyone whose life has just been reshuffled. Among Canadian immigrants, revival breaks out repeatedly. The greatest Southern Baptist growth has been among ethnic communities precisely because transition opens the heart.
blocks.es_reference: Transiciones. Los inmigrantes, los recién casados, los recién jubilados, los nuevos padres, los recién enviudados — cualquiera cuya vida acaba de ser reordenada. Entre los inmigrantes canadienses, el avivamiento estalla repetidamente. El mayor crecimiento bautista del sur ha sido entre comunidades étnicas precisamente porque la transición abre el corazón.

blocks.en: Crisis. Those facing death, divorce, illness, or disaster. Following a flood in Brazil, missionaries gave relief and used the opportunity to plant several churches. Crisis dismantles the illusion of self-sufficiency that closes hearts in easier seasons.
blocks.es_reference: Crisis. Los que enfrentan muerte, divorcio, enfermedad o desastre. Después de una inundación en Brasil, los misioneros dieron auxilio y usaron la oportunidad para plantar varias iglesias. La crisis desmantela la ilusión de autosuficiencia que cierra los corazones en temporadas más fáciles.

blocks.en: The downcast and the poor. Jesus usually went to the poor first and found them most receptive. The rich often think they have no need for God; the poor know they have many needs. The personal evangelist who looks for the burdened, the lonely, and the materially needy will find doors already open. Paul wrote, "Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time" (Colossians 4:5, NKJV). The receptive seasons are short; the wise believer redeems them.
blocks.es_reference: Los abatidos y los pobres. Jesús generalmente iba primero a los pobres y los encontraba más receptivos. Los ricos a menudo piensan que no tienen necesidad de Dios; los pobres saben que tienen muchas necesidades. El evangelista personal que busca al cargado, al solitario y al materialmente necesitado encontrará puertas ya abiertas. Pablo escribió: "Andad sabiamente para con los de afuera, aprovechando bien el tiempo" (Colosenses 4:5, RVG). Las temporadas receptivas son cortas; el creyente sabio las redime.

blocks.en: VII. Dependence on the Holy Spirit
blocks.es_reference: VII. Dependencia del Espíritu Santo

blocks.en: Personal evangelism is not a matter of human persuasion. Jesus promised, "And when He has come, He will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment" (John 16:8, NKJV). Conviction is the work of the Spirit. The believer's role is to speak; the Spirit's role is to convince. This dependence liberates the evangelist from the burden of producing a response. He can speak freely, pray silently, and trust the Spirit to apply the Word.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo personal no es una cuestión de persuasión humana. Jesús prometió: "Cuando él venga, convencerá al mundo de pecado, de justicia y de juicio" (Juan 16:8, RVG). La convicción es obra del Espíritu Santo. El papel del creyente es hablar; el papel del Espíritu es convencer. Esta dependencia libera al evangelista de la carga de producir una respuesta. Puede hablar libremente, orar silenciosamente y confiar en que el Espíritu aplique la Palabra.

blocks.en: Before a conversation, pray for guidance and boldness. During the conversation, listen to the Spirit's leading — perhaps to say more, perhaps to stop, perhaps to ask a different question. After the conversation, pray for the seed to take root. Dependence is not passivity; it is active reliance.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de una conversación, ore por dirección y valentía. Durante la conversación, escuche la dirección del Espíritu Santo — quizás para decir más, quizás para detenerse, quizás para hacer una pregunta diferente. Después de la conversación, ore para que la semilla eche raíces. La dependencia no es pasividad; es confianza activa.

blocks.en: VIII. Avoiding Artificial Evangelism
blocks.es_reference: VIII. Evitar el Evangelismo Artificial

blocks.en: One danger in personal evangelism is artificiality — forcing the conversation, following a script so rigidly that the person feels like a project rather than a person. Paul commanded, "speaking the truth in love" (Ephesians 4:15, NKJV). Love does not manipulate. It respects the other person's dignity and timing. Artificial evangelism often produces shallow responses — a person may give the "right" answers just to end an uncomfortable conversation. Genuine personal evangelism is natural, though not necessarily comfortable. It is honest, not slick. The believer should be himself — not a polished salesman, but a fellow sinner saved by grace. When he shares what God has done for him, with humility and authenticity, the conversation becomes a meeting of souls, not a performance.
blocks.es_reference: Un peligro en el evangelismo personal es la artificialidad — forzar la conversación, seguir un guion tan rígidamente que la persona se sienta como un proyecto en lugar de una persona. Pablo ordenó: "Siguiendo la verdad en amor" (Efesios 4:15, RVG). El amor no manipula. Respeta la dignidad y el tiempo de la otra persona. El evangelismo artificial a menudo produce respuestas superficiales — una persona puede dar las respuestas "correctas" solo para terminar una conversación incómoda. El evangelismo personal genuino es natural, aunque no necesariamente cómodo. Es honesto, no pulido. El creyente debe ser él mismo — no un vendedor refinado, sino un compañero pecador salvado por gracia. Cuando comparte lo que Dios ha hecho por él, con humildad y autenticidad, la conversación se convierte en un encuentro de almas, no en una actuación.

blocks.en: Conclusion: A Lifestyle of Faithful Witness
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión: Un Estilo de Vida de Testimonio Fiel

blocks.en: Personal evangelism is the most basic and natural form of gospel proclamation. It requires clarity, listening, discernment of where the hearer stands, boldness, sensitivity, alertness to receptive seasons, and dependence on the Spirit. It is not reserved for experts; it is the privilege of every believer. The Great Commission is fulfilled one conversation at a time — over coffee, on a walk, in a waiting room, across a dinner table. The believer who prays, prepares, and steps out in faith will find that God opens doors and provides words. The results belong to Him; the faithfulness belongs to us.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo personal es la forma más básica y natural de proclamación del evangelio. Requiere claridad, escucha, discernimiento de dónde está el oyente, valentía, sensibilidad, atención a las temporadas receptivas y dependencia del Espíritu Santo. No está reservado para expertos; es el privilegio de cada creyente. La Gran Comisión se cumple una conversación a la vez — sobre café, en una caminata, en una sala de espera, en una mesa de cena. El creyente que ora, se prepara y da un paso de fe encontrará que Dios abre puertas y provee palabras. Los resultados pertenecen a Él; la fidelidad pertenece a nosotros.

blocks.en: Prayer: Lord, teach us to speak of You naturally, clearly, and lovingly. Give us ears to listen and hearts to discern. Help us recognize whether the person before us is ignorant, indifferent, hostile, interested, or ready, and to respond rightly to each. Lead us to the transitioned, the crisis-stricken, the poor, and the open. Remove the fear of man and replace it with the fear of God. In Jesus' name, Amen.
blocks.es_reference: Oración: Señor, enséñanos a hablar de Ti de manera natural, clara y amorosa. Danos oídos para escuchar y corazones para discernir. Ayúdanos a reconocer si la persona ante nosotros es ignorante, indiferente, hostil, interesada o lista, y a responder correctamente a cada una. Llévanos a los que pasan transiciones, a los azotados por la crisis, a los pobres y a los abiertos. Quita el temor del hombre y reemplázalo con el temor de Dios. En el nombre de Jesús, Amén.

sa.prompt: Define personal evangelism in your own words and explain why it is called 'the most basic form of gospel proclamation.'
sa.model: Personal evangelism is sharing the gospel directly with an individual in conversation, one person at a time. It is called the most basic form of gospel proclamation because it requires no platform, program, or special gift — only a believer and a person who needs Christ. It is how most people actually come to faith, and it is the form available to every Christian in everyday relationships.

sa.prompt: Identify three principles from Jesus' conversation with the Samaritan woman (John 4) that still guide personal evangelism today.
sa.model: Jesus' conversation with the Samaritan woman (John 4) shows enduring principles. He began with a natural point of contact — asking for water — meeting her in an ordinary moment. He listened and engaged her real situation rather than reciting a formula. And he moved from the physical to the spiritual, awakening her sense of need before offering living water. These still guide personal evangelism: start naturally, listen, and lead toward the gospel.

sa.prompt: Name Robinson's five levels of response to the gospel and describe how the evangelist's approach should differ at each level.
sa.model: Robinson's five levels of response are the ignorant, who lack knowledge; the indifferent, who do not care; the hostile, who resist; the interested, who are open; and the ready, who are prepared to respond. The evangelist's approach differs at each: the ignorant need patient teaching, the indifferent need awakening, the hostile need gentleness and prayer, the interested need clear explanation, and the ready need a clear call to commitment.

sa.prompt: Discuss the role of listening (James 1:19) in personal evangelism. Why is listening not optional?
sa.model: James 1:19 says to be swift to hear and slow to speak, and listening is not optional in personal evangelism. Listening lets the witness understand where the person actually is — his questions, objections, and real needs — rather than answering questions no one asked. It builds trust and shows respect, opening the heart to the message. A witness who only talks treats the person as a target; one who listens treats him as a soul.

sa.prompt: Explain the function of CWT's two diagnostic questions in a personal evangelistic conversation.
sa.model: CWT's two diagnostic questions — whether someone is certain he would go to heaven, and what he would say if God asked why He should let him in — function in a personal conversation by gently revealing where the person is resting his hope. The first surfaces his level of assurance; the second exposes whether he trusts his own works or Christ. They open the door to the gospel without argument, letting the person's own answer show his need.

sa.prompt: Describe when people are most receptive to the gospel, using Wayne's three categories: transitions, crisis, and the poor or downcast. Give an example for each.
sa.model: Wayne names three times people are most receptive. Transitions — moves, new jobs, marriage, a new baby — unsettle routine and open people, for example a family that just relocated and is seeking community. Crisis — illness, loss, divorce — strips away self-sufficiency, for example someone facing a frightening diagnosis. And the poor or downcast — those humbled by hardship — are often more open than the comfortable, for example a person who has just lost work. In each, ordinary security has loosened, making the heart more ready for the gospel.

sa.prompt: Distinguish between boldness without sensitivity and sensitivity without boldness. How does Ephesians 4:15 hold them together?
sa.model: Boldness without sensitivity speaks the truth but wounds, driving people away; sensitivity without boldness is kind but never says the hard thing, so the person is never confronted with his need. Ephesians 4:15 holds them together by calling us to speak the truth in love. Truth keeps love from becoming cowardly silence; love keeps truth from becoming a weapon. The faithful witness is both bold and tender at once.

sa.prompt: Explain why the personal evangelist must depend on the Holy Spirit for conviction (John 16:8). Distinguish the evangelist's role from the Spirit's.
sa.model: The personal evangelist must depend on the Holy Spirit for conviction because John 16:8 says it is the Spirit who convicts the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment. The evangelist's role is to speak the truth clearly and lovingly; the Spirit's role is to convince the heart. This distinction frees the witness: he is not responsible to argue someone into belief, only to present Christ faithfully and trust the Spirit to do the inward work he cannot.

sa.prompt: Define artificial evangelism and describe how it fails. Use Ephesians 4:15 to identify the genuine alternative.
sa.model: Artificial evangelism is forced, formulaic, or insincere — treating people as projects and reciting lines without genuine care. It fails because people sense the manipulation and the lack of love, and it misrepresents a gospel that is itself an expression of love. Ephesians 4:15 identifies the genuine alternative: speaking the truth in love. Real evangelism flows from authentic concern for the person, naturally and lovingly, not from a sales technique.

sa.prompt: Synthesize the unit: describe the natural flow of a personal evangelistic conversation from initial connection, through assessment and listening, to a clear call for response.
sa.model: A personal evangelistic conversation flows naturally. It begins with connection — meeting the person in a real, natural point of contact and building trust. It moves through assessment and listening — discerning where he is and hearing his real questions and needs. Then it presents the gospel clearly, fitted to the person. And it ends with a clear call for response — inviting him to repent and trust Christ. Each stage depends on the Spirit and unfolds as a genuine conversation, not a script.
